title: Unit and successive-composition laws for normalized strict coefficient comparisons
statement:
Let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal X)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal Y)$ be a geometric morphism on small sites with left-exact inverse image. For $W=X,Y$ and $a=0,1,2$, let $R^a_{W,\bullet}$ be inverse sequences of commutative ring sheaves, and let $i_W^{ab}:R^a_{W,\bullet}\to R^b_{W,\bullet}$, $a\le b$, satisfy $i^{aa}=1$ and $i^{02}=i^{12}i^{01}$. Let $\phi^a:u^{-1}R^a_{Y,\bullet}\to R^a_{X,\bullet}$ commute with all coefficient and sequence arrows. In module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with actual sheafified tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], set $F_aM=R_X^a\otimes_{u^{-1}R_Y^a}u^{-1}M$ and $S_W^{ab}M=R_W^b\otimes_{R_W^a}M$ levelwise. Let $T_a$ be the signed direct-sum total tensor of arbitrary unbounded cochain complexes [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. A strict system has semilinear chain transitions for every sequence arrow, and strict morphisms commute with them.

Suppose natural chain isomorphisms $k^{ab}:S_X^{ab}F_a\cong F_bS_Y^{ab}$ and $s_W^{ab}:S_W^{ab}T_a\cong T_b(S_W^{ab},S_W^{ab})$, together with their inverses, are strict, and in each level and bidegree have the normalized generator formulas
$$k^{ab}:b\otimes(a\otimes x)\mapsto b i_X^{ab}(a)\otimes(1\otimes x),\quad
(k^{ab})^{-1}:b\otimes(d\otimes x)\mapsto b\phi^b(d)\otimes(1\otimes x),$$
$$s_W^{ab}:b\otimes(x\otimes y)\mapsto(b\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y),\quad
(s_W^{ab})^{-1}:(b\otimes x)\otimes(d\otimes y)\mapsto bd\otimes(x\otimes y).$$
Inverse-image notation is suppressed; the $d$ for $(k^{ab})^{-1}$ belongs to $u^{-1}R_Y^b$.

The multiplication maps
$$U_W^a:S_W^{aa}\cong1,\quad a\otimes x\mapsto ax,\qquad
A_W:S_W^{12}S_W^{01}\cong S_W^{02},\quad d\otimes(b\otimes x)\mapsto d i_W^{12}(b)\otimes x$$
are balanced natural strict chain isomorphisms. Their inverse formulas are $x\mapsto1\otimes x$ and $c\otimes x\mapsto c\otimes(1\otimes x)$ respectively. With composition written in order from right to left, their compatibility equations are
$$F_a(U_Y^a)k^{aa}=U_X^aF_a,\qquad
T_a(U_W^a,U_W^a)s_W^{aa}=U_W^aT_a,$$
$$F_2(A_Y)k^{12}_{S_Y^{01}K}S_X^{12}(k^{01}_K)=k^{02}_K(A_X)_{F_0K},$$
$$T_2(A_W,A_W)s_W^{12}_{S_W^{01}K,S_W^{01}H}S_W^{12}(s_W^{01}_{K,H})
=s_W^{02}_{K,H}(A_W)_{T_0(K,H)}.$$
The successive $k$ routes on $d\otimes(b\otimes(a\otimes x))$ both have value $d i_X^{12}(b)i_X^{02}(a)\otimes(1\otimes x)$ after the displayed source and target identifications. The successive $s_W$ routes on $d\otimes(b\otimes(x\otimes y))$ both have value $(d i_W^{12}(b)\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$. All four equations hold as equalities of strict chain isomorphisms and of their inverse isomorphisms, for arbitrary semilinear transitions, including zero maps, zero rings, nonflat coefficient maps and unbounded complexes.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback; Section Tensor product, section-tensor-product. Agent extraction of returned lem-pur-strict-coefficient-comparison-calculus proof steps 7--8 (multiplication units, balanced associators, successive kappa and sigma equations, inverse equations).

proof.text: We use the actual sheafified tensors, not tensors of global sections. The universal property in [lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal] identifies maps out of a sheaf tensor with restriction-compatible balanced pairings. For sectionwise tensors use the quotient by bilinearity and pure-tensor generation in [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], and descend linear maps by [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]. For an iterated tensor, first define its pairing with the inner presheaf tensor and extend across the inner sheafification by [lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension], then use the outer tensor universal property. Repeating this once more handles three nested tensors. Its uniqueness clauses show that equality on the displayed nested generators implies equality of the resulting sheaf maps. Apply the same argument after restricting the target scalars along each coefficient map; check linearity over the final ring on generators. Thus this test applies to scalar extensions as well. For sources involving $u^{-1}K$, take $x$ to be an arbitrary section of that sheaf; when an inner map on $Y$ is pulled back, apply $u^{-1}$ to its defining equality of morphisms. No claim that sections of $u^{-1}K$ lift globally to $Y$ is needed.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product (balanced tensors and bilinear universal property), and Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, constituents only; agent calculation of multiplication units and successive normalized comparisons.

proof.text: Fix $W$ and a sequence level; abbreviate $R_W^a$ to $R^a$ and $i_W^{ab}$ to $i^{ab}$. For an $R^a$-module $M$, $U(a\otimes x)=ax$ is additive, balanced since $(ar)x=a(rx)$, and $R^a$-linear. Its proposed inverse is linear because $1\otimes rx=r\otimes x$; the two composites are $x\mapsto x$ and $a\otimes x\mapsto1\otimes ax=a\otimes x$. For an $R^0$-module $M$, the formula $A(d\otimes(b\otimes x))=d i^{12}(b)\otimes x$ respects the outer $R^1$ relation since $d i^{12}(t)i^{12}(b)=d i^{12}(tb)$. The inner $R^0$ relation gives $d i^{12}(b i^{01}(r))\otimes x=d i^{12}(b)i^{02}(r)\otimes x=d i^{12}(b)\otimes rx$. For the inverse $B(c\otimes x)=c\otimes(1\otimes x)$, its $R^0$ balancing is $c i^{02}(r)\otimes(1\otimes x)=c\otimes(i^{01}(r)\otimes x)=c\otimes(1\otimes rx)$. Both formulas are additive and $R^2$-linear. Step 1 therefore constructs all four sheaf maps. Now $AB(c\otimes x)=c\otimes x$ and $BA(d\otimes(b\otimes x))=d i^{12}(b)\otimes(1\otimes x)=d\otimes(b\otimes x)$. Step 1 proves the inverse equations. For a module map $h$, either order with $U,A,B$ merely replaces $x$ by $h(x)$; hence these are natural isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product (balanced tensors and bilinear universal property), and Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, constituents only; agent calculation of multiplication units and successive normalized comparisons.

proof.text: Apply Step 2 in every cochain degree. For $U$ both orders with the differential send $a\otimes x$ to $a\,d_Mx$; for $A$ they send $d\otimes(b\otimes x)$ to $d i^{12}(b)\otimes d_Mx$; the inverse formulas give the same check with inserted ones. For a sequence arrow $m\to n$, write $\rho^a$ for its ring maps and $t$ for its semilinear chain transition. Either order with $U$ gives $\rho^a(a)t(x)$, and either order with $A$ gives $\rho^2(d)i_n^{12}(\rho^1(b))\otimes t(x)$, because $\rho^2i_m^{12}=i_n^{12}\rho^1$. For the inverses the common values are $1\otimes t(x)$ and $\rho^2(c)\otimes(1\otimes t(x))$. Thus $U,A$ and their inverses are strict chain maps, including when $t=0$. When evaluated on $T_0(K,H)$ their coefficient multiplication leaves the bidegree unchanged: on $x\in K^p$ it carries the two differential terms separately to the corresponding terms with $d_Kx\otimes y$ and $(-1)^p x\otimes d_Hy$. The direct-sum total in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] is a coproduct in each degree, so equality can be tested on each summand. For $S(Q)$, regard the target as a module over the old ring. The tensor-Hom bijection of [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed] identifies maps from $R^b\otimes_{R^a}Q$ with maps from $Q$ to $\mathcal Hom_{R^a}(R^b,-)$. The coproduct universal property now tests equality on the inclusions of the summands of $Q=T_0$. Apply this bijection twice for $S^{12}S^{01}(T_0)$. Thus bidegree tests suffice on all the scalar-extended totals, without boundedness or a claim that coproduct sections are globally finite sums.

source.place: Tag 012Z, definition-associated-simple-complex, total differential and direct sums; sites-modules.tex Section 03EK, tensor-Hom adjunction and universal property; agent check of coefficient multiplication and arbitrary semilinear transitions.

proof.text: For the first unit equation evaluate on $b\otimes(a\otimes x)$ in $S_X^{aa}F_aK$. The $k^{aa}$ route followed by $F_a(U_Y^a)$ is $ba\otimes(1\otimes x)\mapsto ba\otimes x$; $U_X^aF_a$ gives the same $ba\otimes x$. For the second equation, on $b\otimes(x\otimes y)$ with homogeneous $x,y$, the $s_W^{aa}$ route followed by $T_a(U_W^a,U_W^a)$ gives $(bx)\otimes y=b(x\otimes y)$, which is the value of $U_W^aT_a$. These are balancing and module-action identities, with no change of bidegree. Steps 1 and 3 give equality of the sheaf maps in every degree, hence the two unit equations.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product (balanced tensors and bilinear universal property), and Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, constituents only; agent calculation of multiplication units and successive normalized comparisons.

proof.text: For the successive $k$ equation start with $d\otimes(b\otimes(a\otimes x))$ in $S_X^{12}S_X^{01}F_0K$. Applying $S_X^{12}(k_K^{01})$ gives $d\otimes(b i_X^{01}(a)\otimes(1\otimes x))$. Applying $k^{12}_{S_Y^{01}K}$ gives $d i_X^{12}(b i_X^{01}(a))\otimes(1\otimes(1\otimes x))$. Applying $F_2(A_Y)$ multiplies the two unit coefficients on $Y$, giving $d i_X^{12}(b)i_X^{02}(a)\otimes(1\otimes x)$. In the other order $(A_X)_{F_0K}$ first gives $d i_X^{12}(b)\otimes(a\otimes x)$ and $k_K^{02}$ gives exactly the same value. Here we used multiplicativity of $i_X^{12}$ and the assumed equality $i_X^{12}i_X^{01}=i_X^{02}$; the $Y$ coefficients used in $F_2(A_Y)$ are both $1$. Step 1 establishes equality on the whole source sheaf, in every degree.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product (balanced tensors and bilinear universal property), and Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, constituents only; agent calculation of multiplication units and successive normalized comparisons.

proof.text: For the successive $s_W$ equation start with $d\otimes(b\otimes(x\otimes y))$, $x\in K^p$, $y\in H^q$. The left side successively gives $d\otimes((b\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y))$, then $(d\otimes(b\otimes x))\otimes(1\otimes(1\otimes y))$, then $(d i_W^{12}(b)\otimes x)\otimes(1\otimes y)$. On the right, $(A_W)_{T_0(K,H)}$ gives $d i_W^{12}(b)\otimes(x\otimes y)$ and $s_{W;K,H}^{02}$ gives the same final tensor. No interchange of $x$ and $y$ occurs, so there is no extra Koszul sign. Step 1 gives equality on each sheaf tensor summand and Step 3 gives equality on the arbitrary unbounded direct-sum total.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product (balanced tensors and bilinear universal property), and Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, constituents only; agent calculation of multiplication units and successive normalized comparisons.

proof.text: By hypothesis every $k,s_W$ and its inverse already is a natural strict chain isomorphism, and Step 3 proves this for $U,A$ and their inverses. Thus all routes in Steps 4--6 are well-defined in the category of strict systems. Their componentwise equalities are equalities of strict chain maps, since strictness adds commuting equations to the component maps rather than changing equality. An inverse of an isomorphism is unique: if $P=Q$ then $P^{-1}=P^{-1}QQ^{-1}=Q^{-1}$. Inverting the four equations, with the order of factors reversed, therefore gives exactly the equations of inverse isomorphisms. The proof uses only balancing, addition, multiplication, units and the stated coefficient/sequence squares. It applies to zero rings (where all module sections vanish), nonflat coefficient maps, zero or arbitrary semilinear transitions, and unbounded complexes.
